It can be computed only when the standard deviation is zero
It is always identical to the range

sourceQuote: the coefficient of variation is independent of the unit of measurement
explanationCorrect: The coefficient of variation expresses the standard deviation as a percentage of the mean. Because the mean and standard deviation have the same units, those units cancel, so the coefficient of variation is independent of the unit of measurement.

explanationWrong.A: Variance is already in squared units; the CV is SD as a percentage of the mean, not the square of the variance.
explanationWrong.C: A zero standard deviation would make the CV zero; that is not a requirement for computing it.
explanationWrong.D: The range is a different dispersion measure and is not identical to the CV.

question: What is the specificity of a screening test?

choices.text: The probability the test is positive when the individual has the disease
The probability the individual has the disease when the test is positive
The probability the individual does not have the disease when the test is negative
The probability of the test result being negative when an individual does not have the disease

sourceQuote: the probability of the test result being negative when an individual does not have
explanationCorrect: Specificity is the probability of the test result being negative when an individual does not have the disease. Predictive value negative is the probability of not having the disease when the test is negative.

explanationWrong.A: That definition is sensitivity (positive given disease).
explanationWrong.B: That definition is predictive value positive.
explanationWrong.C: That definition is predictive value negative.

question: In a confidence interval, what is the product of the reliability coefficient and the standard error called?

choices.text: The null hypothesis
The type II error rate
The precision of the estimate, also called the margin of error
The sample size rule of thumb of 30

sourceQuote: It is also called the margin of error
explanationCorrect: The value obtained by multiplying the reliability coefficient and the standard error is referred to as the precision of the estimate. It is also called the margin of error. The center of the interval is the point estimate.

explanationWrong.A: The null hypothesis is a statement tested in hypothesis testing, not the reliability coefficient times SE.
explanationWrong.B: Type II error is failing to reject a false null, not the CI precision term.
explanationWrong.D: A sample size greater than 30 is a rule of thumb for using normal reliability coefficients, not the name of that product.

question: Which indication is typically included in the null hypothesis?

choices.text: Only a directional inequality that forbids equality
An indication of equality (=, ≥, or ≤)
A required p value less than 0.05 written into H0
The investigator’s untestable research suspicion only

sourceQuote: an indication of equality (=, ≥, or ≤) is included in the null hypothesis
explanationCorrect: The null hypothesis is the hypothesis to be tested (typically H0) and is presumed true in the study population. Typically, an indication of equality (=, ≥, or ≤) is included in the null hypothesis.

explanationWrong.A: Equality (including =, ≥, or ≤) is typically included; a hypothesis that forbids all equality is not the usual H0 form given here.
explanationWrong.C: The p value is a result of testing, not a symbol written into H0.
explanationWrong.D: A research hypothesis must be restated as a statistical hypothesis that can be tested.

question: When the null hypothesis is true but the investigator rejects it, which error has been committed?

choices.text: A type I error
A type II error
A nonrejection-region error
A reliability-coefficient error

sourceQuote: When the null hypothesis is true, but the statistical decision is to reject
explanationCorrect: When the null hypothesis is true, but the statistical decision is to reject the null hypothesis, the investigator has committed a type I error. The probability of a type I error is the significance level α.

explanationWrong.B: A type II error occurs when the null is not true and the decision is not to reject it.
explanationWrong.C: Falling in the nonrejection region leads to not rejecting H0, which is not a type I error.
explanationWrong.D: The reliability coefficient is used in confidence intervals, not as the name of this error.

question: What is the p value for hypothesis testing?

choices.text: The predetermined sample size needed for 80% power
The probability of seeing a test statistic as extreme as or more extreme than the value observed
The reliability coefficient from a t distribution only
The coefficient of determination ranging from 0 to 1

sourceQuote: the probability of seeing a test statistic that is as extreme as or more extreme
explanationCorrect: The p value is the probability of seeing a test statistic that is as extreme as or more extreme than the value of the test statistic observed. Reporting the p value is more informative than reporting only the reject/not-reject decision.

explanationWrong.A: Sample size and power are not the definition of the p value given here.
explanationWrong.C: The reliability coefficient is a confidence-interval quantity, not the p value.
explanationWrong.D: The coefficient of determination evaluates a regression line, not hypothesis-test p values.

question: In simple linear regression, which statement about the independent variable X is correct?

choices.text: It is plotted on the vertical axis and cannot be preselected
It is the outcome whose values are never controlled
It is usually controlled by the investigator, and its values may be preselected
It must be a qualitative attribute such as sex

sourceQuote: Variable X is usually controlled by the investigator, and its values may be preselected
explanationCorrect: In simple linear regression, independent variable X is usually controlled by the investigator, and its values may be preselected. X is assigned to the horizontal axis and dependent variable Y to the vertical axis.

explanationWrong.A: X is assigned to the horizontal axis, and its values may be preselected.
explanationWrong.B: Y is the dependent outcome; X may be controlled and preselected.
explanationWrong.D: The example uses age and forced expiratory volume, quantitative variables; X is not required to be qualitative.

question: How is the coefficient of determination interpreted when evaluating a regression equation?

choices.text: It ranges from 0 to 1; values closer to 1 mean observations lie closer to the regression line
It ranges from –1 to 1 and equals the slope b
It is significant only when it equals the intercept a
It is identical to the standard error of the mean

sourceQuote: The coefficient of determination ranges from 0 to 1
explanationCorrect: The coefficient of determination describes the relative magnitude of scatter about the regression line and ranges from 0 to 1. The closer it is to 1, the closer the observations lie to the regression line.

explanationWrong.B: The –1 to 1 range is given later for the correlation coefficient, not the coefficient of determination.
explanationWrong.C: The intercept a is a separate parameter; it is not the significance rule for the coefficient of determination.
explanationWrong.D: The coefficient of determination is not the standard error of the mean.

question: If simple linear regression or correlation identifies a strong linear relationship between two variables, what caution does the chapter emphasize?

choices.text: The relationship may be used as proof of cause and effect
That relationship should not be mistaken as evidence of cause and effect
The variables need not be measured on the same unit of association
A correlation of zero proves a perfect inverse causal effect

sourceQuote: that relationship should not be mistaken as evidence of cause and effect
explanationCorrect: Even when analysis identifies a strong linear relationship, that relationship should not be mistaken as evidence of cause and effect. Also, X and Y must be measured on the same unit of association.

explanationWrong.A: The passage warns against treating the relationship as cause and effect.
explanationWrong.C: X and Y must be measured on the same unit of association.
explanationWrong.D: If ρ = 0, the two variables are not linearly correlated; that is not a perfect inverse causal effect.

question: In a chi-square test, what does a larger X2 quantity indicate?

choices.text: Better agreement between observed and expected frequencies
That the variables must be continuous rather than categorical
Poorer agreement between observed and expected frequencies, which can lead to rejection of the null hypothesis
That expected frequencies may be ignored

sourceQuote: the poorer the agreement, the greater the quantity of X2
explanationCorrect: X2 measures agreement between observed and expected frequencies: the poorer the agreement, the greater X2. A large enough X2 leads to rejection of the null hypothesis.

explanationWrong.A: Greater X2 means poorer, not better, agreement.
explanationWrong.B: Chi-square is described as suitable because the variables are categorical.
explanationWrong.D: Expected frequencies are essential; they are the counts expected if the null is true.

question: When expected frequencies are too small, a chi-square test would not be appropriate. What threshold and alternative are suggested?

choices.text: Chi-square is preferred when any expected cell is zero only if X2 is small
A small X2 always rejects the null hypothesis
Fisher’s exact test is used only when expected counts exceed 50
Some writers suggest all expected values should be greater than 5 or 10; otherwise an alternative such as Fisher’s exact test should be used

sourceQuote:
that all expected values should be
greater than 5 or 10. Otherwise,
explanationCorrect: X2 measures disagreement between observed and expected frequencies; a large enough X2 rejects the null, and under the null X2 follows a chi-square distribution. If expected frequencies are too small (suggested >5 or 10), use an alternative such as Fisher’s exact test.

explanationWrong.A: Small expected frequencies make chi-square inappropriate; a small X2 indicates better agreement, not automatic rejection.
explanationWrong.B: A large enough X2 leads to rejection; poorer agreement yields greater X2.
explanationWrong.C: Fisher’s exact test is the alternative when expected values are too small, not when they exceed 50.

question: Compared with parametric tests, a stated advantage of nonparametric tests is which of the following?

choices.text: They always require knowing the exact form of the population distribution
They apply when data are merely rankings or classifications that may not be a strong enough measurement level for parametric tests
They estimate the population mean under normality as their only use
Chi-square is classified here as a parametric test of the mean

sourceQuote:
tests. First, nonparametric tests apply when the data are merely
rankings or
explanationCorrect: Parametric tests estimate or test population parameters (e.g., mean or proportion) and require knowing the population distribution form. Nonparametric tests apply to rankings or classifications that may be too weak for parametric methods. Chi-square is excepted from the parametric grouping in this discussion.

explanationWrong.A: Knowing the population distribution form is a parametric requirement, not a nonparametric advantage.
explanationWrong.C: Estimating the population mean under a known distribution is the parametric setting.
explanationWrong.D: Chi-square is noted as an exception among tests described so far, i.e., not grouped with the parametric tests.

question: What is the only requirement stated for using the sign test, and what raw data enter the test statistic?

choices.text: The variable must be categorical; the data are class-interval frequencies
The variable must be continuous; the raw data are plus and minus signs
The sample size must exceed 1,000; the data are regression residuals
The distribution must be normal; the data are z scores

sourceQuote: The only requirement for using the sign test is that the variable be continuous
explanationCorrect: The sign test focuses on the median. The only requirement is that the variable be continuous. The raw data used in the test statistic are plus and minus signs; values equal to the hypothesized median are dropped.

explanationWrong.A: The sign test requires a continuous variable, not categorical class frequencies.
explanationWrong.C: Large samples are described as making nonparametric tests time consuming, not as a requirement of the sign test.
explanationWrong.D: Normality is not required; plus and minus signs are used, not z scores.

question: Which listed statement about a frequency distribution is identified as not true?

choices.text: An observation in a data set can belong to more than one interval
Frequency as a statistical measure can be included in a frequency distribution
Relative frequency as a statistical measure can be included in a frequency distribution
Cumulative relative frequency as a statistical measure can be included in a frequency distribution

sourceQuote: An observation in a data set can belong to more than one interval
explanationCorrect: A self-assessment item asks which statement is not true about frequency distribution and lists that an observation can belong to more than one interval. Frequency, relative frequency, and cumulative relative frequency are listed as measures that can be included.

explanationWrong.B: Frequency is listed as a measure that can be included in a frequency distribution.
explanationWrong.C: Relative frequency is listed as a measure that can be included.
explanationWrong.D: Cumulative relative frequency is listed as a measure that can be included.

question: In the screening-test table of 100 individuals, how many had disease present and a positive test result?
sourceQuote: The following table shows 100 individuals cross-classified according to
explanationCorrect: In the table, among those with disease present, 30 had a positive test and 20 had a negative test. Forty positives occurred among those with disease absent.

explanationWrong.A: Ten is the number with disease absent and a negative test.
explanationWrong.B: Twenty is the number with disease present and a negative test.
explanationWrong.D: Forty is the number with disease absent and a positive test.

question: Which statement about a test statistic is listed as true among the self-assessment options?

choices.text: If the test statistic falls into the nonrejection region, the test is said to be significant
The rejection region can be on only one tail of the distribution
Researchers typically prefer higher levels of significance
A test statistic can assume different values when different samples are drawn from the population

sourceQuote: A test statistic can assume different values when different samples are drawn
explanationCorrect: One listed true statement is that a test statistic can assume different values when different samples are drawn from the population. Significance is associated with the rejection region, and tests may be one-sided or two-sided.

explanationWrong.A: The test is said to be significant if the statistic falls into the rejection region, not the nonrejection region.
explanationWrong.B: The rejection region may include one tail or two tails.
explanationWrong.C: The passage does not state that researchers typically prefer higher significance levels as a true claim.

question: Which relationship between the correlation coefficient and the coefficient of determination is stated in this passage?

choices.text: The correlation coefficient equals the square of the coefficient of determination
The correlation coefficient is always equal to the intercept a
Investigators can preselect values of the dependent variable for simple linear regression
The absolute value of the correlation coefficient equals the square root of the coefficient of determination

sourceQuote: The absolute value of the correlation coefficient equals the square root of
explanationCorrect: A listed statement is that the absolute value of the correlation coefficient equals the square root of the coefficient of determination. Regression and correlation analyses are not said to determine causal relationships.

explanationWrong.A: The stated relationship is the square root, not the square, of the coefficient of determination.
explanationWrong.B: The intercept a is not identified as equal to the correlation coefficient.
explanationWrong.C: Investigators may preselect the independent variable, not the dependent variable, for simple linear regression.

question: What is the sensitivity of a test, according to the chapter answers?

choices.text: The probability of a negative result when the individual does not have the disease
The probability of the test result being positive when an individual has the disease
The probability of having the disease when the test is positive
The probability of not having the disease when the test is negative

sourceQuote: The sensitivity of a test is the probability of the test result being positive
explanationCorrect: The sensitivity of a test is the probability of the test result being positive when an individual has the disease. Specificity is the probability of a negative result when the individual does not have the disease.

explanationWrong.A: That definition is specificity.
explanationWrong.C: That definition is predictive value positive.
explanationWrong.D: That definition is predictive value negative.

question: What raw data are used to calculate the test statistic for the sign test?

choices.text: Chi-square expected frequencies only
The coefficient of determination
Plus and minus signs
Reliability coefficients from the standard normal distribution

sourceQuote: only the positive and negative signs of the data
explanationCorrect: The sign test takes into consideration only the positive and negative signs of the data. The raw data used in the calculation of the test statistic are plus and minus signs.

explanationWrong.A: Expected frequencies belong to chi-square tests, not the sign-test statistic described here.
explanationWrong.B: The coefficient of determination evaluates a regression equation, not the sign test.
explanationWrong.D: Reliability coefficients are used for confidence intervals, not the sign-test statistic.

question: Which study design is described as able to establish a cause-and-effect relationship between variables?

choices.text: A well-designed randomized controlled trial (RCT)
Any retrospective observational study
A case report of a single patient
A cross-sectional cohort study without randomization

sourceQuote: Well-designed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) can establish a cause-and-effect relationship
explanationCorrect: Well-designed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) can establish a cause-and-effect relationship between variables. Retrospective studies are ideally able to identify an association between variables.

explanationWrong.B: Retrospective studies are described as identifying association, not establishing cause and effect.
explanationWrong.C: Case reports are not credited here with establishing cause and effect.
explanationWrong.D: Cohort studies may be prospective, cross-sectional, or retrospective; RCTs, not unrandomized cohorts, are credited with cause and effect.

question: Clinical research, as defined in this chapter, refers to studies conducted in which subjects and seeking answers in which domain?

choices.text: In vitro cell lines seeking only reimbursement questions
Animal models seeking manufacturing specifications
Humans seeking to answer a question regarding health care
Computer simulations seeking only coding accuracy

sourceQuote: Clinical research refers to studies conducted in humans seeking to answer a
explanationCorrect: Clinical research refers to studies conducted in humans seeking to answer a question regarding health care. It includes studies evaluating medical disease prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.

explanationWrong.A: The definition is studies in humans regarding health care, not in vitro reimbursement research.
explanationWrong.B: The subjects are humans, not animal manufacturing studies.
explanationWrong.D: The definition is human health-care questions, not coding simulations.

question: What can a case report establish regarding causality?

choices.text: A definitive cause-and-effect relationship equivalent to an RCT
Case reports cannot establish a causal relationship but may be the first evidence of a previously unknown relationship
Proof that confounding variables have been eliminated
That the described intervention is always prospective

sourceQuote: Case reports cannot establish a causal relationship but may often be the first evidence
explanationCorrect: A case report retrospectively describes a specific clinical case or a limited number of cases. Case reports cannot establish a causal relationship but may often be the first evidence of a previously unknown or unrecognized relationship.

explanationWrong.A: Case reports cannot establish a causal relationship.
explanationWrong.C: The passage does not credit case reports with eliminating confounding.
explanationWrong.D: A case report is described as retrospective, not always prospective.

question: A case series differs from a single case report in which way?

choices.text: It always includes randomization and a concurrent control group
It can never be retrospective
It reports on a group of patients with similar clinical presentations or exposures rather than a single or very limited number of cases
It is identical to a double-blind pivotal Phase III trial

sourceQuote: This type of study is similar to a case report although it
explanationCorrect: A case series is like a case report but describes a group with similar presentations or exposures. Knowing design terminology helps clinicians interpret how a published study was conducted.

explanationWrong.A: Lack of control and randomization is discussed in the following passage as a limitation of case series.
explanationWrong.B: The next passage notes a case series may be retrospective or prospective.
explanationWrong.D: Pivotal trials are a different experimental design.

question: A cohort study is described as essentially the same as a randomized controlled trial except for which feature?

choices.text: Cohort studies always randomize exposure at baseline
The absence of randomization
Cohort studies never include a comparison group
Cohort studies cannot be conducted over time

sourceQuote: The lack of a control group and randomization limits the
explanationCorrect: Case series lack a control group and randomization, limiting causal inference and rigorous statistics. Cohort studies select participants by characteristics, compare exposed versus unexposed over time, and resemble RCTs except they lack randomization.

explanationWrong.A: Absence of randomization is the stated distinction from RCTs.
explanationWrong.C: A different set of patients or the general population serves as control.
explanationWrong.D: Participants are compared over time.

question: How does this passage distinguish bias from confounding variables?

choices.text: Bias is random error; confounding is always introduced systematically by the investigator
They are identical terms for placebo effect
Bias denotes systematic error; confounding variables are not systematically introduced but may affect the outcome and generally cannot be controlled completely
Confounding occurs only in randomized trials; bias occurs only in case reports

sourceQuote: Bias denotes systematic error within clinical investigations. Bias is distinct
explanationCorrect: Bias denotes systematic error within clinical investigations and is distinct from confounding variables. Confounding variables are not systematically introduced but may affect the outcome and generally cannot be controlled completely (e.g., concurrent medications).

explanationWrong.A: Bias is systematic error, not random error; confounding is not described as systematically introduced.
explanationWrong.B: Bias and confounding are distinguished, not treated as identical.
explanationWrong.D: The inability to randomize is a major source of bias in cohort studies; the distinction is not limited to RCTs versus case reports.

question: A stated difference between case-control studies and cohort studies in this comparison is which of the following?

choices.text: Case-control studies match controls on predefined characteristics such as age or sex and are always retrospective
Case-control studies are always prospective randomized experiments
Cohort studies never include participants who have the disease
RCTs are defined as always retrospective chart reviews

sourceQuote:
Another
difference is that case-control studies are always retrospective.
Randomized controlled trial
explanationCorrect: Case-control studies compare diseased participants with matched controls (e.g., age or sex) and are always retrospective. RCTs prospectively randomly assign eligible participants to treatment or control groups.

explanationWrong.B: Case-control studies are always retrospective, not prospective randomized trials.
explanationWrong.C: Both case-control and the cohort comparison include a group with disease versus without.
explanationWrong.D: RCTs prospectively assign participants randomly after inclusion criteria are met.

question: In a parallel RCT as defined here, study participants typically do which of the following?

choices.text: Cross over to the opposite arm at a planned midpoint in all such trials
Serve as their own controls for every outcome
Receive the assigned treatment or control for the entire trial, with outcomes compared between groups at the conclusion
Avoid randomization and self-select placebo or active drug

sourceQuote:
participants receive the
assigned treatment or control for the entire trial in
explanationCorrect: In a parallel RCT, participants are randomized to a treatment or control arm (standard treatment, no treatment, usual care, or placebo) and typically remain on the assigned intervention for the entire trial; outcomes are compared between groups at the end. Parallel and crossover are the two most common RCT subtypes.

explanationWrong.A: Crossover is a different RCT subtype; parallel design keeps the assigned arm for the entire trial.
explanationWrong.B: Patients serving as their own controls characterizes crossover design, not this parallel description.
explanationWrong.D: Participants are randomized; they do not self-select arm assignment.

question: In a crossover randomized controlled trial, what is the purpose of the washout period?

choices.text: To increase carryover so that residual effects can be measured as the primary endpoint
To randomize newly enrolled patients into parallel arms
To convert an acute, unstable condition into a chronic disease
To allow return to the same baseline state and avoid a carryover or residual effect between treatments

sourceQuote: This time period is referred to as a “washout” period
explanationCorrect: A return to the same baseline state is needed for crossover designs. This frequently requires a period of no treatment or usual treatment between study periods to avoid a carryover or residual effect, referred to as a washout period.

explanationWrong.A: The washout is used to avoid carryover, not to increase it.
explanationWrong.B: Washout is an interval between crossover periods, not a method of parallel-arm randomization.
explanationWrong.C: Crossover designs are limited to stable, chronic, or episodic conditions; washout does not convert acute disease into chronic disease.

question: How are randomized controlled trials ranked in the hierarchy of medical literature described here?

choices.text: They have a high weighting in the ranks of medical literature
They are ranked below case reports for scientific rigor
They cannot be interpreted without a crossover design
They are excluded from diagrams of scientific rigor

sourceQuote: RCTs have a high weighting in the ranks of medical literature
explanationCorrect: RCTs have a high weighting in the ranks of medical literature. Understanding RCT design aids interpretation and application of new literature to practice.

explanationWrong.B: The passage states RCTs have high weighting, not ranking below case reports.
explanationWrong.C: Parallel and other RCT designs exist; crossover is not required for interpretation.
explanationWrong.D: Figure 20-3 is described as illustrating scientific rigor of particular study designs, including RCTs.

question: When applying RCT results to practice, what must be true of enrolled study participants?

choices.text: They may violate exclusion criteria if the sample size is large
They need not resemble the population to which results will be applied
They must be representative of the target population, meet all inclusion criteria, and not have exclusion-criteria characteristics
They must include every patient in the population with the disease

sourceQuote: Study participants must be representative of the population to which the results
explanationCorrect: Study participants must be representative of the population to which the results are to be applied. Enrolled patients must meet all predetermined inclusion criteria and must not have any exclusion-criteria characteristics.

explanationWrong.A: Patients must not have exclusion-criteria characteristics; large sample size does not waive that rule.
explanationWrong.B: Representativeness of the target population is required.
explanationWrong.D: Sampling is necessary because enrolling every patient in the population is not feasible.

question: Does randomization ensure that participant characteristics such as sex, weight, and race are equally divided between groups, and what process can accomplish that equal division?

choices.text: Yes; blinding after enrollment is sufficient
No; stratification, a grouping that occurs before randomization, can be used
Yes; intention-to-treat analysis equalizes baseline traits
No; only per-protocol analysis can balance those traits

sourceQuote: Randomization does not ensure that study participant characteristics
explanationCorrect: Randomization does not ensure that characteristics such as sex, weight, and race are equally divided. Stratification is a grouping that occurs before randomization to accomplish that division; retrospective grouping is often called subgroup analysis.

explanationWrong.A: Blinding decreases bias in outcome assessment; it is not the method given for balancing baseline characteristics.
explanationWrong.C: Intention-to-treat is an analysis approach for dropouts, not a method to equalize baseline traits.
explanationWrong.D: Per-protocol analysis excludes protocol deviations; it is not the stratification process described.

question: What is statistical power in a randomized controlled trial?

choices.text: The probability of avoiding a false-negative study result
The probability of committing a type I error
The margin of error of a confidence interval
The washout duration needed to prevent carryover

sourceQuote: statistical power is the probability of avoiding a false-negative study result
explanationCorrect: Inadequate numbers decrease statistical power, so a real difference may be missed. Statistical power is the probability of avoiding a false-negative study result. Greater expected treatment differences and less outcome variability reduce the number of participants needed.

explanationWrong.B: The type I error probability is the significance level α, not statistical power.
explanationWrong.C: Margin of error is a confidence-interval precision term, not power.
explanationWrong.D: Washout prevents carryover in crossover trials; it is not the definition of power.

question: Regarding RCT sample size and controls, which statement matches the text?

choices.text: Larger expected treatment differences always require more participants
Greater outcome variability always reduces the number of participants needed
In a crossover design, patients never serve as their own control
Greater expected difference and less outcome variability each reduce the number of participants needed; in a crossover design, patients serve as their own control

sourceQuote:
the
greater the expected difference between the study treatments, the fewer the
explanationCorrect: The greater the expected difference, the fewer participants needed; fewer are also needed when outcome variability is lower. Power based on those estimates should be reported. In crossover RCTs, patients serve as their own control.

explanationWrong.A: Greater expected difference means fewer, not more, participants.
explanationWrong.B: Less variability means fewer participants, not more.
explanationWrong.C: Crossover patients serve as their own control.

question: To avoid compromising blinding, a placebo should have dosage-form properties (color, shape, taste) identical to active treatment. When may placebos be unsuitable, and what is the placebo effect?

choices.text: Placebos are ethically required in every RCT; they never affect outcomes
Placebos may be unsuitable for ethical reasons, in which case active or usual treatment is used; the placebo effect is an effect on the study outcome despite an inactive substance
Only historical controls can replace an unethical placebo
Blinding is improved by making placebo look different from active drug

sourceQuote:
the
placebo should have dosage form properties (e.g., color, shape, taste) that
explanationCorrect: Control groups may receive standard treatment, no treatment, usual care, or placebo in crossover and parallel RCTs. Identical appearance protects blinding. Placebo effect is an outcome change despite inactivity. If placebo is ethically unsuitable, use active or usual treatment. Follow-up must be long enough for safety and/or efficacy.

explanationWrong.A: Placebos are not suitable for all RCTs because of ethics; they can affect outcomes (placebo effect).
explanationWrong.C: Historical controls are not offered here as the ethical substitute; active or usual treatment is.
explanationWrong.D: Identical, not different, dosage-form properties protect blinding.

question: How does intention-to-treat analysis handle patients who withdraw after randomization?

choices.text: It excludes all patients with any missing visit
It reassigns dropouts to whichever arm had a better outcome
It includes all patients in their randomized groups and uses data up to the point of withdrawal
It analyzes only participants with no protocol deviations

sourceQuote: This method includes all patients as a member of their respective study group
explanationCorrect: Intention to treat includes all patients as members of their respective randomized groups regardless of protocol completion. Data up to the point of withdrawal are used. Per protocol excludes data from participants with significant protocol deviations.

explanationWrong.A: ITT uses data up to withdrawal rather than excluding all patients with missing visits.
explanationWrong.B: Patients remain in their randomized groups; they are not reassigned by outcome.
explanationWrong.D: Analyzing only those without significant deviations is the per-protocol method.

question: Which question is listed among those used in critical appraisal of a clinical trial?

choices.text: Were all confounding variables proven impossible in every participant?
Did the groups have similar baseline characteristics at the start of the study?
Was the study budget large enough to guarantee a positive result?
Did investigators omit clinically important outcomes to shorten follow-up?

sourceQuote: Did the groups have similar baseline characteristics at the start of the study
explanationCorrect: Critical appraisal questions include whether groups had similar baseline characteristics at the start of the study, whether participants and personnel were blinded, and whether groups were treated equally aside from the experimental interventions.

explanationWrong.A: Proving all confounding impossible is not listed as an appraisal question.
explanationWrong.C: Study budget guaranteeing a positive result is not an listed appraisal item.
explanationWrong.D: The checklist asks whether all clinically important outcomes were considered, not whether they were omitted.

question: Which of the following is listed as a descriptive statistic commonly used in characterizing data from observational studies?

choices.text: Arithmetic mean
Bayesian posterior odds
Kaplan–Meier hazard ratio
Intention-to-treat p value

sourceQuote: Which of the following are descriptive statistics commonly used in characterizing data from observational studies?
explanationCorrect: A self-assessment item lists arithmetic mean, mode, and range among descriptive statistics commonly used in characterizing observational-study data, with normality listed as another choice.

explanationWrong.B: Bayesian posterior odds are not listed among those descriptive statistics.
explanationWrong.C: A Kaplan–Meier hazard ratio is not listed among those descriptive statistics.
explanationWrong.D: An intention-to-treat p value is not listed among those descriptive statistics.

question: Which clinical trial design is identified as evaluating intrasubject effects between two or more study treatments?

choices.text: Parallel
Case series
Cohort
Crossover

sourceQuote: Which of the following clinical trial designs evaluates intrasubject effects between two or more study treatments?
explanationCorrect: A self-assessment item identifies a crossover design as evaluating intrasubject effects between two or more study treatments. Parallel, case series, and cohort designs are listed as alternatives.

explanationWrong.A: Parallel design compares separate groups rather than the named intrasubject comparison.
explanationWrong.B: A case series is not the design named for intrasubject treatment comparisons.
explanationWrong.C: A cohort study is not the design named for evaluating intrasubject effects.

question: Regarding sample size in randomized controlled trials, which listed statement is correct?

choices.text: Increased sample size reduces statistical power
Increased sample size is needed for a crossover design versus a parallel design
Decreased sample size is needed when the expected difference in outcome between groups is large
Decreased sample size is needed where large variability exists in the study outcome being measured

sourceQuote: Decreased sample size is needed when the expected difference in outcome between groups is large
explanationCorrect: A listed statement is that decreased sample size is needed when the expected difference in outcome between groups is large. Large outcome variability increases, rather than decreases, the sample size needed.

explanationWrong.A: Inadequate numbers decrease power; increasing sample size does not reduce power.
explanationWrong.B: Crossover designs typically need fewer, not more, participants because of less variability.
explanationWrong.D: Large variability increases the number of participants needed.

question: Which of the following is listed as a quantity used to calculate a sample size?

choices.text: Desired statistical power
The pharmacy’s average wholesale markup
The number of continuing-education credits offered
The journal’s impact factor

sourceQuote: Which of the following are used to calculate a sample size?
explanationCorrect: A self-assessment item asks which quantities are used to calculate a sample size and lists desired statistical power, estimated effect size, and variability and experimental error among the choices.

explanationWrong.B: Average wholesale markup is not listed as a sample-size input.
explanationWrong.C: Continuing-education credits are not listed as a sample-size input.
explanationWrong.D: Journal impact factor is not listed as a sample-size input.

question: According to the chapter answers, case reports are always which type of study?

choices.text: Randomized
Observational
Prospective
Placebo-controlled

sourceQuote: Case reports are always observational. Prospective designs, randomization,
explanationCorrect: Case reports are always observational. Prospective designs, randomization, and controls are study characteristics commonly used with randomized controlled trials and are not associated with case reports.

explanationWrong.A: Randomization is not associated with case reports.
explanationWrong.C: Case reports are not described as prospective designs.
explanationWrong.D: Controls are not associated with case reports.

question: In a double-blind study, who is unaware of the subject treatment?

choices.text: Subjects only
Subjects and investigators
Investigators and data analysis personnel only, not subjects
Data analysis personnel and subjects, but not investigators

sourceQuote: Subjects and investigators are unaware of the subject treatment in a double-blind study
explanationCorrect: Subjects and investigators are unaware of the subject treatment in a double-blind study. In a single-blind study, only the subjects are unaware. A triple-blind study blinds all persons who come in contact with the study procedures or data.

explanationWrong.A: Subjects only describes single-blind, not double-blind.
explanationWrong.C: Double-blind includes subjects and investigators, not investigators and analysts excluding subjects.
explanationWrong.D: Investigators are also unaware in a double-blind study.

question: Regarding stratification in clinical trials, which statement is supported?

choices.text: It ensures equal distribution of selected subject characteristics, requires a larger number of patients, can be used in parallel and crossover designs, and is performed before randomization
It is performed after randomization so that groups can be unbalanced on purpose
It cannot be used in a crossover study
Decreased sample size is needed when outcome variability is large

sourceQuote:
and crossover study designs. Stratification is
performed before randomization.
13. C. Decreased
explanationCorrect: Stratification ensures equal distribution of selected characteristics, needs more patients, works in parallel and crossover designs, and is done before randomization. Decreased sample size is appropriate when the expected between-group difference is large or in crossover designs (patients as their own controls); larger samples increase power when variability is large.

explanationWrong.B: Stratification is performed before randomization.
explanationWrong.C: It can be used in both parallel and crossover designs.
explanationWrong.D: Increased, not decreased, sample size is needed when variability in the outcome is large.

question: Which control type cannot be used in a randomized clinical trial according to this answer, and which withdrawal-handling approach is called inappropriate?

choices.text: Placebo cannot be used; purging withdrawn subjects’ data is required
Usual care cannot be used; only per-protocol analysis is allowed
Historical controls cannot be used; purging data on withdrawal and analyzing only protocol completers is inappropriate
Standard treatment cannot be used; intention-to-treat is forbidden

sourceQuote:
controls. Historical controls cannot be used in a randomized
clinical trial.
15.
explanationCorrect: RCTs can use standard treatment, usual care, and placebo as controls, but historical controls cannot. Withdrawals can be handled with ITT, ITT plus per-protocol, or per-protocol categorization by reason; purging data and including only completers is inappropriate. Critical appraisal includes validity, applicability, and basic design.

explanationWrong.A: Placebo is an allowed RCT control; purging completers-only data is inappropriate, not required.
explanationWrong.B: Usual care is an allowed control; ITT is an accepted withdrawal-handling method.
explanationWrong.D: Standard treatment is an allowed control; ITT is described as an appropriate analytic option.

question: Which of the following is identified as a potential confounding variable?

choices.text: Exclusion of patients with severe forms of the disease being studied
A predetermined inclusion criterion listed in the protocol
A subject’s concurrent medications
Random assignment to treatment arms

sourceQuote: Potential confounding variables include a subject’s concurrent medications
explanationCorrect: Potential confounding variables include a subject’s concurrent medications, medical complications during the study period, and study dropouts. Exclusion of patients with severe disease is not a confounding variable because it can be specified in inclusion and exclusion criteria.

explanationWrong.A: Excluding severe disease is not a confounding variable because it can be controlled by eligibility criteria.
explanationWrong.B: A protocol inclusion criterion is a designed eligibility rule, not a listed confounder.
explanationWrong.D: Random assignment is a design feature to support valid comparisons, not a listed confounder.

question: Which statement about confounders and sample-size inputs matches this answer key?

choices.text: Exclusion of patients with severe disease is a classic uncontrolled confounder
Sample size is generally calculated from the probability that results will affect clinical practice
Concurrent medications, on-study complications, and dropouts cannot be confounders

Potential confounders include concurrent medications, medical complications during the study, and dropouts; exclusion of severe disease can be controlled and is not a confounding variable; sample size uses power, effect size, and variability, not the probability of affecting practice

sourceQuote:
Exclusion of patients with severe forms of the disease being
studied is not a confounding variable
explanationCorrect: Confounders include concurrent medications, complications, and dropouts. Excluding severe disease is not a confounder because it can be controlled. Sample size uses desired power, estimated effect size, and variability/experimental error—not the chance results will affect practice.

explanationWrong.A: Exclusion of severe disease is specifically said not to be a confounding variable because it can be controlled.
explanationWrong.B: Probability of affecting clinical practice is not generally used to calculate sample size.
explanationWrong.C: Those items are listed as potential confounding variables.

question: Intention-to-treat analysis is described as including data from which patients?

choices.text: Only patients who completed the protocol exactly as written
All patients regardless of whether they completed the protocol
Only patients who experienced the primary outcome
Only patients whose follow-up duration was limited by the study budget

sourceQuote:
A. The intention-to-treat analysis includes data from all patients regardless of
whether
explanationCorrect: ITT includes data from all patients regardless of protocol completion. In a parallel RCT, patients do not serve as their own controls and generally receive only one study treatment. Follow-up duration is set by the outcome, long-term safety, and time to observe an effect—not the study budget.

explanationWrong.A: Including only completers is not ITT as defined here.
explanationWrong.C: ITT is not restricted to those who experienced the outcome.
explanationWrong.D: Study budget is not a scientific factor in determining follow-up duration.

question: Which citation is included among the additional resources for using articles about therapy or prevention?

choices.text: Guyatt GH, Sackett DL, Cook DJ. Users’ guides to the medical literature
Beauchamp TL, Childress JF. Principles of Biomedical Ethics
Daniel WW. A Foundation for Analysis in the Health Sciences
Garner BA, ed. Black’s Law Dictionary

sourceQuote: Guyatt GH, Sackett DL, Cook DJ. Users’ guides to the medical literature
explanationCorrect: The additional resources include Guyatt GH, Sackett DL, Cook DJ, Users’ guides to the medical literature. II. How to use an article about therapy or prevention, JAMA 1994.

explanationWrong.B: Beauchamp and Childress appear in the ethics chapter resources, not this clinical-trial list.
explanationWrong.C: Daniel’s biostatistics text is cited in the biostatistics chapter, not here.
explanationWrong.D: Black’s Law Dictionary is a pharmacy-law resource, not this list.

question: Which set correctly lists the principles of bioethics given in this chapter?

choices.text: Autonomy, beneficence, nonmaleficence, and justice
Compassion, discernment, trustworthiness, integrity, and conscientiousness
Veracity, fidelity, and paternalism only
Confidentiality and profitability only

sourceQuote: The principles of bioethics are autonomy, beneficence, nonmaleficence, and justice
explanationCorrect: The principles of bioethics are autonomy, beneficence, nonmaleficence, and justice. Compassion, discernment, trustworthiness, integrity, and conscientiousness are the virtues of bioethics.

explanationWrong.B: That list is the virtues of bioethics, not the four principles.
explanationWrong.C: Veracity, fidelity, and paternalism are not the four principles named here.
explanationWrong.D: Confidentiality and profitability are not the four principles named here.

question: Which practice is listed as an ethical requirement when accepting patients for a clinical study?

choices.text: Withholding the study purpose to protect the protocol
Informing the patient about the purpose of the study, the risks associated with it, and the right to discontinue participation
Requiring participants to remain in the study until the sponsor consents to withdrawal
Disclosing identifiable subject data without consent if it would speed enrollment

sourceQuote: Informing the patient about the purpose of the study, the risks associated with it
explanationCorrect: Ethical research practices include informing the patient about the purpose of the study, the risks associated with it, and the right to discontinue participation, and recruiting with honesty and integrity.

explanationWrong.A: The purpose of the study must be disclosed, not withheld.
explanationWrong.C: Patients have the right to discontinue participation; remaining until the sponsor consents is not listed.
explanationWrong.D: Intellectual property and honest reporting are required; unauthorized disclosure of identifiable data is not an ethical practice listed here.

question: What is identified as the primary set of principles that guide ethical pharmacy practice?

choices.text: The principles of medical ethics
Employer productivity quotas alone
State tax codes
International trade treaties

sourceQuote: the primary set of principles that guide ethical practice of pharmacy are the principles of medical ethics
explanationCorrect: As members of the health care team, the primary set of principles that guide ethical practice of pharmacy are the principles of medical ethics. This chapter concentrates on the ethical framework for pharmacy practice in the United States.

explanationWrong.B: Employer quotas are not identified as the primary ethical principles.
explanationWrong.C: State tax codes are not the guiding ethical framework named here.
explanationWrong.D: International trade treaties are not the primary ethical principles for pharmacy practice named here.

question: Nonmaleficence, often expressed as “do no harm,” refers to which kinds of harm?

choices.text: Only deliberate, malicious harm
Only physical injury from an approved drug’s labeled effect
Deliberate malicious harm and also harm from inefficiency, poorly designed systems, carelessness, and tasks beyond one’s expertise
Only economic harm to the pharmacy owner

sourceQuote: refers not only to deliberate, malicious harm but also to harm
explanationCorrect: Nonmaleficence refers not only to deliberate, malicious harm but also to harm from inefficiency, poorly designed systems, carelessness, and performance of tasks beyond one’s level of expertise. Duties can include supervising assistants and students and maintaining knowledge and skills.

explanationWrong.A: The duty extends beyond deliberate malicious harm.
explanationWrong.B: The examples include system and skill failures, not only labeled pharmacologic effects.
explanationWrong.D: The duty is about harm to those entrusted to one’s care, not merely the owner’s economics.

question: How is integrity defined among the virtues of bioethics?

choices.text: Placing appropriate weight on competing duties and knowing when to compromise
The willingness to act consistently on one’s moral commitments, even when uncomfortable or at personal risk
Reaching decisions without influence from the patient’s feelings
Concealing errors to preserve public confidence

sourceQuote: Integrity involves the willingness to act consistently on one’s moral commitments
explanationCorrect: Integrity involves the willingness to act consistently on one’s moral commitments, even when uncomfortable or in the presence of personal risk. Conscientiousness is placing appropriate weight on competing duties.

explanationWrong.A: That definition is conscientiousness, not integrity.
explanationWrong.C: Discernment asks whether one is responding to the patient’s feelings and needs rather than one’s own, not ignoring the patient.
explanationWrong.D: Trustworthiness requires honesty and transparency, not concealing errors.

question: Who developed the Code of Ethics for Pharmacists that embodies expected U.S. pharmacist behaviors, and in what year?

choices.text: The Joint Commission in 1992
The Drug Enforcement Administration in 1970
The American Pharmacists Association (APhA) in 1994
The Food and Drug Administration in 1938

sourceQuote: which was developed by the American Pharmacists Association (APhA) in 1994
explanationCorrect: The Code of Ethics for Pharmacists was developed by the American Pharmacists Association (APhA) in 1994 and is endorsed by all the other major American pharmacy associations.

explanationWrong.A: The Joint Commission’s 1992 mandate concerned hospital ethics mechanisms, not authorship of this Code.
explanationWrong.B: DEA did not develop the APhA Code of Ethics for Pharmacists in 1970.
explanationWrong.D: FDA’s 1938 FDCA role is unrelated to authorship of this professional code.

question: The covenant expressed in the Oath of a Pharmacist is identified as the basis of which professional relationship?

choices.text: The manufacturer–wholesaler contracting relationship
The pharmacist–board of pharmacy inspection relationship only
The insurer–formulary committee relationship
The pharmacist–patient relationship

sourceQuote: is the basis of the pharmacist –patient relationship. 2.
explanationCorrect: Pharmacists honor patient trust by working with the health care team; that covenant, expressed in the Oath of a Pharmacist, is the basis of the pharmacist–patient relationship.

explanationWrong.A: Supply-chain contracting is not the covenant named here.
explanationWrong.B: Regulatory inspection is not the relationship grounded in the Oath in this passage.
explanationWrong.C: Payer formulary work is not the named basis of the oath covenant.

question: Respect for patient autonomy in the Code of Ethics requires pharmacists to do which of the following?

choices.text: Avoid prejudging patients on stereotypes and encourage questions and participation in health decisions
Apply the same counseling script to every patient regardless of health literacy
Withhold information to preserve dignity when language barriers exist
Base integrity on occasional, situation-dependent ethics rather than consistent moral convictions

sourceQuote: patient on the basis of stereotypes or unfounded generalizations.
explanationCorrect: Pharmacists must consider health literacy, language, and disability; avoid stereotyped prejudgment; and promote self-determination by encouraging questions and shared decisions.

explanationWrong.B: The passage requires appropriate consideration of health literacy, not a uniform script.
explanationWrong.C: Language barriers call for appropriate consideration, not concealment of information.
explanationWrong.D: Integrity means being consistently guided by moral and ethical convictions.

question: If a pharmacist’s knowledge and abilities are inadequate to meet a particular patient’s needs, what professional behavior is expected?

choices.text: Continue without assistance to avoid undermining confidence
Seek consultation from colleagues or refer the patient to a more qualified practitioner
Tell the patient that other professionals are incompetent if their approach differs
Place personal financial gain ahead of referral

sourceQuote: pharmacists are expected to recognize when their knowledge and abilities are inadequate
explanationCorrect: Pharmacists are expected to recognize when their knowledge and abilities are inadequate and either seek consultation from colleagues or refer the patient to another, more qualified practitioner. They should avoid behavior that raises questions in the patient’s mind about other professionals’ competence because of differing beliefs and values.

explanationWrong.A: Continuing without help when knowledge is inadequate is contrary to the stated duty.
explanationWrong.C: Pharmacists should avoid raising questions about other professionals’ competence because of differences in approach.
explanationWrong.D: The Code emphasizes patient welfare, not placing personal gain ahead of needed referral.

question: In the Oath of a Pharmacist, which concerns are identified as primary?

choices.text: The welfare of humanity and relief of suffering
The profitability of the practice site
Loyalty to a single manufacturer
Avoiding all change in patient care

sourceQuote: the welfare of humanity and relief of suffering my primary concerns
explanationCorrect: The Oath states: I will consider the welfare of humanity and relief of suffering my primary concerns. It also includes a lifelong obligation to improve professional knowledge and competence.

explanationWrong.B: Practice-site profitability is not identified as a primary oath concern.
explanationWrong.C: Loyalty to a manufacturer is not an oath primary concern.
explanationWrong.D: The Oath includes embracing and advocating changes that improve patient care.

question: How should professional codes of ethics be used when addressing ethical dilemmas?

choices.text: As catalogs of moral information that professionals can simply consult for answers
As tools for reasoning that guide professionals with the fundamental ethical commitments of the profession
As substitutes for moral judgment that eliminate all uncertainty
As binding legal statutes enforced by the FTC

sourceQuote: They are not intended to be catalogs of moral information that professionals can simply consult
explanationCorrect: Professional codes of ethics are tools for reasoning out ethical dilemmas. They are not intended to be catalogs of moral information that professionals can simply consult for answers, because ethically difficult situations inevitably require moral judgment.

explanationWrong.A: The passage explicitly rejects using codes as catalogs that supply ready answers.
explanationWrong.C: Difficult situations still require moral judgment; codes do not eliminate all uncertainty.
explanationWrong.D: Codes of ethics are professional tools, not FTC-enforced statutes as described here.

question: A pharmacist who owns shares in a pharmaceutical company and serves on a hospital pharmacy and therapeutics committee faces which ethical problem?

choices.text: A potential conflict of interest in evaluating that company’s products versus similar products from other vendors
A mandatory duty to vote only for that company’s products
An obligation to conceal the share ownership from the committee
No ethical issue if the shares are profitable

sourceQuote: This situation would represent a potential conflict of interest in cases where such pharmacists serve
explanationCorrect: Pharmacists who own shares in a pharmaceutical company may be biased in evaluating that company’s products. This would represent a potential conflict of interest when such pharmacists serve on a pharmacy and therapeutics committee.

explanationWrong.B: The passage describes a potential COI to be avoided or managed, not a duty to favor the company.
explanationWrong.C: Conflicts should be managed with integrity and transparency, not concealment.
explanationWrong.D: Profitability does not erase the described conflict of interest.

question: A pharmacist paid by a manufacturer to present on that company’s drug may face which ethical problem?

choices.text: A legal requirement to refuse all continuing-education speaking
An obligation to hide all risks because disclosure is never allowed
A tendency to speak more favorably about the medication or minimize its risks for fear of losing future paid opportunities
A mandate to hire relatives as a condition of the speaking contract

sourceQuote: Pharmacists who are paid by pharmaceutical companies to give drug-related
explanationCorrect: Industry-paid presentations create pressure to speak favorably or minimize risks. Industry-funded research and hiring or recommending family or friends irrespective of qualifications are additional conflict-of-interest examples.

explanationWrong.A: The issue is bias in content, not a ban on all speaking.
explanationWrong.B: Minimizing risks is the ethical problem, not a required practice.
explanationWrong.D: Nepotism in hiring is a separate COI example, not a speaking-contract mandate.

question: Why are conflicts of interest said not to be ethical dilemmas in the strict sense?

choices.text: The morally right action is usually unclear, as in a true dilemma
The right course is usually clear and consistent with the person’s moral code but conflicts with personal or financial interests
COI never create morally dangerous situations
Professionals have no duty to avoid conflicts that are likely to develop

sourceQuote: COI do not pose ethical dilemmas because they do not produce situations
explanationCorrect: In a COI the right action is typically clear but opposed by self-interest. Humans tend to put their own interests first, so pharmacists have duties to avoid COI whenever possible, including likely future conflicts. Supervising relatives may impair objectivity.

explanationWrong.A: Unclear right action defines a dilemma; COI are distinguished from that.
explanationWrong.C: The text says COI do produce morally dangerous situations.
explanationWrong.D: There is an explicit duty to avoid COI, including situations likely to develop.

question: When conflicts of interest are unavoidable, serving on committees such as institutional review boards is described as whose duty?

choices.text: A duty of every individual pharmacist regardless of role
A duty of the profession, but not of all individual pharmacists
A duty only of pharmaceutical manufacturers
A duty only of state governors

sourceQuote: a duty of the profession (but not of all individual pharmacists) is to assist peers
explanationCorrect: When COI are unavoidable, pharmacists must recognize and manage them, including cooperating with IRBs that review human-subjects research. Assisting peers by serving on such committees is a duty of the profession but not of all individual pharmacists.

explanationWrong.A: The passage distinguishes a profession-level duty from a duty of every individual pharmacist.
explanationWrong.C: IRB service is framed as a pharmacy-profession duty, not a manufacturer-only duty.
explanationWrong.D: Governors are not assigned this IRB-service duty here.

question: A pharmacist whose conscience forbids a normally expected task should take which step regarding employment and patient communication?

choices.text: Inform supervisors of the need for accommodation before accepting employment, or as soon as reasonably possible after the belief develops, and refrain from discussing the conflicting beliefs with patients
Discuss the conflicting beliefs at length with each affected patient
Refuse to notify supervisors so that staffing plans remain unchanged
Require patients to adopt the pharmacist’s beliefs before any referral

sourceQuote: informing their supervisors of their need for accommodation before accepting employment
explanationCorrect: Objecting pharmacists should inform supervisors of the need for accommodation before accepting employment (or as soon as reasonably possible after the belief develops), cooperate so patient care is not disrupted, and refrain from discussing the conflicting beliefs with patients.

explanationWrong.B: They should refrain from discussing the conflicting beliefs with patients.
explanationWrong.C: Supervisors must be informed so systems can prevent disruption of care.
explanationWrong.D: Patients retain the right to products and services according to their own informed choices.

question: From the principle of autonomy, which right do fully informed patients who possess decision-making capacity have?

choices.text: No right to decline any clinician-recommended drug
A right to decline treatment, even life-sustaining treatment
A right that applies only after an irreversible coma
A right limited to declining nonprescription products

sourceQuote: have the right to decline treatment —even life-sustaining treatment
explanationCorrect: It follows from autonomy that fully informed patients who possess decision-making capacity have the right to decline treatment—even life-sustaining treatment. Beneficence requires that suffering patients be cared for with sensitivity.

explanationWrong.A: Capacity-holding informed patients may decline treatment, including life-sustaining treatment.
explanationWrong.C: People are encouraged to name surrogates because incapacity can happen unexpectedly at any age; the right is not limited to irreversible coma.
explanationWrong.D: The stated right is not limited to nonprescription products.

question: As of 2017 in this chapter’s account, physician-assisted suicide for terminally ill patients was legal in how many states plus the District of Columbia?

choices.text: Two states only, and not the District of Columbia
All fifty states
Six states and the District of Columbia
The federal system exclusively, with no state laws

sourceQuote: physician-assisted suicide for terminally ill patients is legal in six states and the District of Columbia
explanationCorrect: The chapter states that as of 2017, physician-assisted suicide for terminally ill patients is legal in six states and D.C.

explanationWrong.A: The count given is six states plus D.C., not two states without D.C.
explanationWrong.B: It is not described as legal nationwide.
explanationWrong.D: The legalization described is state (and D.C.) law, not a sole federal regime.

question: Because palliative care, hospice, and physician-assisted suicide all involve prescription medications, pharmacists are advised to do which of the following?

choices.text: Consider their own beliefs, values, and emotional needs, which may lead to conscientious objection
Ignore personal values because end-of-life care never creates ethical tension
Refuse all opioid dispensing during a national addiction crisis, without individual assessment
Treat hospice as identical to physician-assisted suicide under federal compounding law

sourceQuote: beliefs, values, and emotional needs regarding participating in end-of-life care.
explanationCorrect: Reflection on personal values can guide practice setting and which end-of-life services a pharmacist is ethically comfortable providing; conscientious objection may be considered. A separate section notes the opioid-addiction crisis.

explanationWrong.B: The passage states this is an area where personal values may conflict with patient care.
explanationWrong.C: Illegitimate opioid-seeking is a risk to consider, not a blanket refusal rule in this excerpt.
explanationWrong.D: Palliative care, hospice, and PAS are distinguished, not equated.

question: How should prescription drug monitoring programs (controlled substances databases) be used, and how do their requirements vary?

choices.text: They should be used routinely; requirements and procedures vary by state
They are optional federal systems with identical procedures in every state
They should be ignored to avoid prejudicial stereotyping
They replace the duty to respect other team members’ roles

sourceQuote: Requirements and procedures for prescription drug monitoring programs vary by state
explanationCorrect: Systems to detect drug abuse and diversion, such as computerized statewide or regional PDMP networks, should be used routinely. Requirements and procedures for prescription drug monitoring programs vary by state.

explanationWrong.B: Requirements and procedures vary by state; they are not described as identical nationwide.
explanationWrong.C: Pharmacists should avoid prejudicial stereotyping but should still use PDMPs routinely and watch for warning signs of illicit acquisition.
explanationWrong.D: Interprofessional respect is a separate duty and is not replaced by PDMP use.

question: Pharmacists are ethically bound to promote a drug product only for which indications?

choices.text: Any use suggested by a sales representative
Only indications that maximize pharmacy profit
Indications approved by the FDA or for which there is ample evidence in the professional and scientific literature (off-label use)
Indications listed solely in consumer advertisements

sourceQuote: promote a drug product only for the indications for which it has been approved
explanationCorrect: Pharmacists are ethically bound to promote a drug product only for FDA-approved indications or those with ample evidence in the professional and scientific literature (off-label use). Misrepresenting therapeutic merit is unethical, and clinically significant adverse effects should be disclosed.

explanationWrong.A: Sales-representative suggestions are not the ethical standard given.
explanationWrong.B: Drugs should be promoted on the basis of patients’ needs rather than a desire to profit.
explanationWrong.D: Consumer advertisements are not the stated basis for ethical promotion.

question: Because pharmaceutical practice affects the environment, which related duty is listed?

choices.text: Providing environmentally safe disposal of drugs and health-related products
Encouraging dumping of unused medicines into municipal sewers
Ignoring environmental effects when teaching trainees
Maximizing packaging waste to protect product identity

sourceQuote: providing environmentally safe disposal of drugs and health-related products
explanationCorrect: Responsible practice must consider the effect of drugs and health-related products on the natural world. Related duties may include providing environmentally safe disposal of drugs and health-related products, supporting environmentally friendly business practices, and raising trainee awareness of inappropriate dumping.

explanationWrong.B: The duty is environmentally safe disposal, not dumping into sewers.
explanationWrong.C: Pharmacists should raise awareness in students and trainees of environmental effects of inappropriate dumping.
explanationWrong.D: Supporting environmentally friendly business practices is listed, not maximizing waste.

question: Related environmental duties of responsible pharmacy practice, as listed, include which of the following?

choices.text: Requiring all unused drugs to be flushed to inactivate them
Prohibiting any discussion of environmental effects with trainees
Ignoring landfill disposal because drugs have no environmental impact
Environmentally safe disposal of drugs, environmentally friendly business practices, and raising trainee awareness of dumping medications in sewage systems and landfills

sourceQuote:
environmental effects of inappropriate dumping of
medications in sewage systems and landfills
explanationCorrect: Duties include environmentally safe disposal, supporting environmentally friendly business practices, and raising awareness of inappropriate dumping of medications in sewage systems and landfills.

explanationWrong.A: Flushing is not prescribed as the required inactivation method; dumping in sewage is cited as a problem.
explanationWrong.B: Raising awareness in students and trainees is listed as a duty, not prohibited.
explanationWrong.C: The text states practice must consider environmental effects of drugs and health-related products.

question: Therapeutic misconception occurs when which misunderstanding arises among clinical-trial enrollees?

choices.text: Investigators believe research exists only to benefit the individual patient
Patients enroll hoping the study drug will benefit them and are not fully aware they may not benefit from the study at all
Subjects refuse informed consent because research never includes patients
IRBs require that every protocol guarantee personal therapeutic benefit

sourceQuote:
the individual patient. Therapeutic misconception occurs when patients
who enroll in clinical
explanationCorrect: The goal of research is to advance medical knowledge, whereas treatment aims to benefit the individual patient. Therapeutic misconception is when enrollees hope the study drug will help them and do not fully realize they may not benefit; careful informed consent can help avoid it.

explanationWrong.A: Investigators’ beliefs are not the definition given; the misconception is on the enrollee’s side.
explanationWrong.C: Research subjects are frequently also patients; informed consent is the safeguard, not refusal.
explanationWrong.D: The text does not say IRBs must guarantee personal benefit.

question: Research involving human subjects must be approved by which body, and what right must subjects be told they have?

choices.text: A marketing committee; the right to guaranteed therapeutic benefit
The state board of pharmacy only; no withdrawal right
A hospital ethics committee acting as a court; the right to payment
An institutional review board (IRB); the right to discontinue participation without penalty

sourceQuote: Research involving human subjects must be approved by an institutional review board
explanationCorrect: Research involving human subjects must be approved by an IRB, which protects welfare by reviewing design and materials. Subjects should be made aware of their right to discontinue participation without penalty, and identifiable information must be kept confidential.

explanationWrong.A: IRB approval is required; guaranteed therapeutic benefit is not the stated right.
explanationWrong.B: IRB approval is required, and subjects have a right to discontinue without penalty.
explanationWrong.C: IRBs review research; they are not described as courts that guarantee payment.

question: Which statement about conflicts of interest is listed as correct in this self-assessment?

choices.text: Conflicts of interest are inherently unethical
Dual relationships are rarely a source of conflicts of interest if everyone involved is careful
Conflicts of interest arise when persons or organizations have multiple interests and are in a position to make decisions that give them an unfair advantage
Conflicts of interest arise only after people take unfair advantage of their position

sourceQuote: Conflicts of interest arise when persons or organizations have multiple interests and are in a position
explanationCorrect: The listed correct statement is that conflicts of interest arise when persons or organizations have multiple interests and are in a position to make decisions that give them an unfair advantage. COI are not described here as inherently unethical in themselves.

explanationWrong.A: The option that COI are inherently unethical is listed as an incorrect alternative.
explanationWrong.B: Dual relationships are not dismissed as rare sources of COI in the keyed statement.
explanationWrong.D: The correct framing is the position to decide among multiple interests, not only after unfair advantage has already been taken.

question: When a drug is scarce, which listed course is identified as the best ethical action?

choices.text: Distribute on a first-come, first-served basis until the supply is exhausted
Keep all the supply for the pharmacist’s own customers or patients
Place the needs of the broader community ahead of the pharmacist’s own patients without balancing
Balance the needs of society and individual patients in making allocation decisions

sourceQuote: Balance the needs of society and individual patients in making decisions
explanationCorrect: When availability is scarce, the best listed ethical course is to balance the needs of society and individual patients in making decisions regarding allocation of the drug.

explanationWrong.A: First-come, first-served until exhaustion is listed as an inferior alternative.
explanationWrong.B: Keeping the entire supply only for one’s own patients is listed as an inferior alternative.
explanationWrong.C: Placing community needs entirely ahead of one’s own patients, without balancing, is listed as an inferior alternative.

question: What is the purpose of a medical ethics committee, according to this self-assessment?

choices.text: Regulate biomedical research
Help health care professionals in dealing with ethical difficulties
Prescribe a course of action that is final and binding
Provide legal advice

sourceQuote: Help health care professionals in dealing with ethical difficulties
explanationCorrect: The purpose of a medical ethics committee is to help health care professionals in dealing with ethical difficulties. It is not described here as regulating research, issuing a final binding order, or providing legal advice.

explanationWrong.A: Regulating biomedical research is not the listed purpose of a medical ethics committee.
explanationWrong.C: The committee is not said to prescribe a final and binding course of action.
explanationWrong.D: Providing legal advice is not the listed purpose.

question: Which statement regarding interprofessional teamwork is identified as an ethical action of a pharmacist?

choices.text: Withhold certain patient information from other members of the team
Raise concerns or disagreements with other members of the team
Disregard the views of another member of the team
Inform a patient that he or she questions the competence or judgment of other members of the team

sourceQuote: Raise concerns or disagreements with other members of the team
explanationCorrect: An ethical action is to raise concerns or disagreements with other members of the team. Withholding information, disregarding others’ views, and telling the patient one questions teammates’ competence are listed as contrary options.

explanationWrong.A: Withholding patient information from the team is not the listed ethical action.
explanationWrong.C: Disregarding another member’s views is not the listed ethical action.
explanationWrong.D: Informing the patient that one questions teammates’ competence is not the listed ethical action.

question: What is the first duty of a pharmacist who is aware that another pharmacist is functioning while impaired?

choices.text: Protecting patients from potential harm
Ignoring the situation to respect professional autonomy
Waiting until a patient is actually injured before acting
Discussing the impairment only with the affected pharmacist’s patients

sourceQuote: Protecting patients from potential harm is the first duty of a pharmacist
